chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Mabbah, from so-and-so ibn Humayd, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and consulted him regarding
the name of his child, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Name him with names from servitude.' He said, 'Which names are these?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abd al-Rahman.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ: Abd al-Rahman (Servant of the Most Merciful)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for naming children in Shia Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs the inquirer to select names denoting 'servitude' (al-‘ubudiyyah), specifically recommending 'Abd al-Rahman' as the ideal exemplar. This guidance underscores the Shia theological emphasis on humility and the recognition of human dependence on the Divine, aligning the child’s identity with the core attribute of mercy. Such naming conventions serve as a perpetual reminder of the bond between the creator and the created, reinforcing spiritual devotion from early life.
